    Statements of the large-indecomposable theorems #

    This file uses only Mathlib. It fixes the vocabulary of the manuscript Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture and states its three principal results:

    • TheoremA (Theorem A = Theorem 5.1): a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field admits a representation embedding F : D → Mod A from the Kronecker modules without simple injective summand, sending finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, commuting with arbitrary direct sums and filtered colimits, and preserving the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules;
    • CorollaryDimension (Corollary 1.1): such an algebra has an indecomposable module of every infinite dimension (the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture over algebraically closed fields);
    • CorollaryRadical (Corollary 5.3): these modules can be chosen with End(M)/rad End(M) ≅ k and (rad End(M))ⁿ = 0 for one n independent of the dimension.

    ClosedUnderColimits records that D has arbitrary coproducts and filtered colimits, so the preservation statements of Theorem A are not vacuous.

    Conventions follow the manuscript. Modules are left modules. A Kronecker module (V, W; a, b) has V at the source vertex, W at the target vertex and arrow maps a b : V → W; it is a functor from WalkingParallelPair to ModuleCat k. Dimensions are cardinals (Module.rank). All types live in one universe u.

    Kronecker modules #

    source
    @[reducible, inline]
    abbrev LargeIndecomposable.Statement.Kron (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Type (u + 1)

    Kronecker modules: representations (V, W; a, b) of the Kronecker quiver 1 ⇉ 2, as diagrams V ⇉ W of k-vector spaces of arbitrary dimension, that is, functors from the walking parallel pair to k-vector spaces. The space V sits at zero, W at one, and the arrow maps are a (left) and b (right). Morphisms are pairs (g, h) with h a = a' g and h b = b' g (natural transformations).
